title: [FancyZones] App zone history entry is used for another monitor after a display change
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Stable

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

I can't force the condition: a monitor must get the handle value (`HMONITOR`) another monitor had. So I give an observation, not steps.

On a laptop with one external monitor, one display active at a time, FancyZones ran for days across switches. After a switch the log has `[trace] DeviceId changed`, then this pair:

```
[info] Get <app> zone history on work area: <laptop panel>
[info] App zone history found on the work area <external monitor>
```

The second line prints the id of the stored entry. This pair with two different monitors occurs 65 times on 9 days (14 September to 10 October 2026), in both directions.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

An app zone history entry is used only for the monitor it was stored for.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

A lookup of an app's zones for one monitor returns an entry with the id of the other monitor. I observed this in the log only, not in window positions.

### Additional Information

From the code on main:

- `AppZoneHistory::SetAppLastZones` stores a new entry with the work area's monitor handle. An entry loaded from `app-zone-history.json` has none.
- `operator==` for `FancyZonesDataTypes::MonitorId` compares two ids that both have a handle by the handle alone.
- `FancyZones::ShouldWorkAreasBeRecreated` logs `DeviceId changed` when the work area found by a monitor handle has another device id.
- So the entry of one monitor equals the work area of the other. `SetAppLastZones` can overwrite its layout id and zones, and `GetAppLastZoneIndexSet` returns its zones when the layout ids match.
- Not observed (the log has no handle values): after a monitor gets another handle, its entry doesn't equal its work area, and the next snap adds a second entry.

A fix with unit tests is in commit [6e7bdf2fc](https://github.com/vdvoorder/PowerToys/commit/6e7bdf2fc93f1ae561c7858c890ab7c619e40372) on my fork, based on main at `a5e83e5e2`:

- `SetAppLastZones` sets the monitor handle in the id of a new entry to null. So no stored entry has a handle, and every comparison of a stored entry with a work area uses the serial numbers and the device ids, as for the entries loaded from the file.
- It doesn't change the comparison of monitor ids, the update of an existing entry, or the applied layouts.
- Entries already in `app-zone-history.json` aren't repaired.
- Two monitors of the same model are now told apart as after a restart: by their serial numbers when both are set and differ, otherwise only when both their instance ids and their display numbers differ.
- The new class `AppZoneHistoryMonitorHandleUnitTests` has three tests, which fail without the change. With the change, the FancyZones unit tests (Release x64, each test class in its own `vstest.console.exe` process) give 299 of 300 passed and 0 failed; `WindowProcessingUnitTests::NonRootWindow` had no result after a crash of `vstest.console.exe`, as on main without the change. The build has 0 warnings.

### Other Software

No other software is involved.

title: Command Palette: extension log messages are retained forever (unbounded `LogMessages`) — multi-GB memory growth with a chatty extension
body:
## Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 (Release). Command Palette package 0.12.12365.0.
The code below is unchanged in v0.102.2933.0 and on `main`.

## Installation method

Installed via Winget

## Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install an extension that calls `ExtensionHost.LogMessage` often. For me this was
   **SteamPal for Command Palette** 0.0.2.0 (StontyTech) with Steam running. It logs
   `Error during data model update: ...` in a loop.
2. Leave Command Palette running for a few hours or days.
3. Watch `Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe` memory in Task Manager.

Any extension that logs in a loop should reproduce this, because the host keeps
every message an extension sends.

## ✔️ Expected Behavior

Extension log messages use bounded memory: either a capped history, or they are
written to the log file and dropped.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

Command Palette memory grows without limit. It reached about **10 GB** on my
machine, and it grows every session for as long as the extension keeps logging.

Each session's Command Palette log
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\CmdPal\Logs\0.101.2362.0\`) reaches
**126–155 MB**. The current one has 818,650 lines, and 818,608 of them are
`AppExtensionHost.cs::LogMessage`:

```text
715,334  [SteamCmdPalExtension] Error during data model update: Error: Duplicate `id` in protoc…
 93,733  [SteamCmdPalExtension] Error during data model update: The requested operation require…
  9,147  [SteamCmdPalExtension] Error during data model update: The JSON value could not be con…
```

### Cause (from the source at v0.102.2933.0)

1. **Every message is added to a static collection, and nothing ever removes one.**
   `AppExtensionHost.LogMessages` is a `static ObservableCollection<LogMessageViewModel>`
   ([AppExtensionHost.cs#L20](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.102.2933.0/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/AppExtensionHost.cs#L20)).
   `ProcessLogMessage` adds a view model for each message
   ([L109-L121](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.102.2933.0/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/AppExtensionHost.cs#L109-L121)).
   No code in `src/modules/cmdpal` removes items from it, clears it or caps it.
2. **Each retained view model holds the extension's COM object, not just its text.**
   `LogMessageViewModel` keeps an `ExtensionObject<ILogMessage>`
   ([LogMessageViewModel.cs#L12](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.102.2933.0/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/LogMessageViewModel.cs#L12),
   [L19](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.102.2933.0/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/LogMessageViewModel.cs#L19)).
   For an out-of-process extension, that is one live cross-process reference per
   message, so the extension's process pays for every message too.
3. **The log page keeps a second copy and inserts each one at the front of a `List<T>`.**
   `LogMessagesPage` subscribes to `CollectionChanged`
   ([LogMessagesPage.cs#L21](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.102.2933.0/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/Commands/LogMessagesPage.cs#L21))
   and runs `_listItems.Insert(0, li)` for each message
   ([L36](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.102.2933.0/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/Commands/LogMessagesPage.cs#L36)).
   Every insert shifts the whole list, so the cost of each message grows with
   the backlog. `RaiseItemsChanged` fires on every message.

### Suggested fix

- Cap `LogMessages` and `_listItems` with a ring buffer (for example the last
  1,000 messages); the file log already keeps the full history.
- In `LogMessageViewModel`, copy `Message` and `State` out and release the
  `ILogMessage` instead of keeping the `ExtensionObject`.
- Append rather than `Insert(0, …)`, and reverse the order when reading.
- Optionally, collapse repeated identical messages from one extension
  ("repeated N times").

## Additional Information

- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300
- Possibly the same symptom as #48975 and #48978, which report Command Palette
  using 32 GB of RAM with no cause found.

**Possibly related, not confirmed: a system-wide stall right after exiting Command
Palette.** It has happened three times. The extension log records `Dispose` at the
moment I exit. For the next ~15–17 minutes:

- No new process starts properly. Explorer windows, Task Manager, terminals,
  PowerShell 5.1 and 7, and `tasklist`/WMI all hang.
- Windows Search filter hosts are killed every 30 s (event 10024).
- The Group Policy Client service times out while starting (event 7009).
- Programs that were already running keep working at first.

It then clears on its own. `WerFault.exe` was running from about 80 s after the
exit until the stall cleared. No crash event (1000/1002) was logged, and no
Command Palette or extension process was alive mid-stall. One guess is that
tearing down hundreds of thousands of retained cross-process `ILogMessage`
references at exit ties up COM for every other process. I can't prove that. I'm
happy to test a build with a capped `LogMessages`.

## Other Software

Third-party Command Palette extensions installed: SteamPal for Command Palette
0.0.2.0 (the one flooding the log), Port, Event Viewer, Process Killer, Temp
Cleaner, PaletteShell, Definition.

title: DSC: PowerToysConfigure throws "PowerToys installation wasn't found" on 4-part release versions
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Preview

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Installer, Settings

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 per-user with WinGet (`Microsoft.PowerToys`).
1. Apply a WinGet configuration that uses the `Microsoft.PowerToys.Configure/PowerToysConfigure` resource, for example:

   ```yaml
   - resource: Microsoft.PowerToys.Configure/PowerToysConfigure
     directives:
       description: Configure PowerToys
     settings:
       Awake:
         Enabled: true
   ```

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The resource finds the installation and applies the settings.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The unit fails with:

```text
PowerToysConfigure
  The configuration unit failed while attempting to apply the desired state.
PowerToys installation wasn't found.
```

The generated module locates the installation by an exact match on the uninstall registry entry (`Microsoft.PowerToys.Configure.psm1`, line 3192 in 0.101.2362.0):

```powershell
Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -eq "PowerToys (Preview)" -and $_.DisplayVersion -eq "0.101.2362" }
```

The MSI registers the 4-part version, so the comparison never matches:

```text
DisplayName     : PowerToys (Preview)
DisplayVersion  : 0.101.2362.0
InstallLocation : C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\PowerToys\
```

### Additional Information

Cause, as far as I can trace it: since #49414 moved releases to 4-part versions, `$(var.Version)` and so the MSI `DisplayVersion` carry four parts. [`DSCGeneration.cs`](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/dsc/PowerToys.Settings.DSC.Schema.Generator/DSCGeneration.cs) still writes `GetProductVersion()` into the `.psm1` lookup as three parts (line 224), and appends `.0` only for the `.psd1` `ModuleVersion` (line 397). Matching on `[version]` instead of the string, or applying the same `.0` normalization to the lookup, would fix it.

The generator is unchanged on `main`, so 0.102.x releases should be affected too; I have only verified 0.101.2362.0.

GitHub, PowerToys auto-update, WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set up **Mouse Without Borders** between two Windows 10 (`10.0.19045`, 64-bit) machines (or a Windows 10 and Windows 11 machine) on the same LAN.
2. Move the mouse cursor across the screen boundary to control the remote machine, or trigger a desktop switch / hidden cursor transition.
3. Observe repeated connection drops, cursor snapping back to the local machine, and continuous reconnect loops in the Mouse Without Borders logs (`Log_*.log`).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

- During initialization (`InitAndCleanup.Init()`), `MouseWithoutBorders` should accurately probe whether `InputInjector.InjectMouseInput` works on the current OS/desktop, and fall back to Win32 `SendInput` (`SendInput64`) if `InputInjector` is unavailable or throws a `COMException`.
- During runtime mouse movement (`InputSimulation.SendInputEx`), if `Injector.InjectMouseInput(...)` throws a `COMException` (such as `0x8007007A` `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER` or `0x80070005` `E_ACCESSDENIED`), it should gracefully fall back to `NativeMethods.SendInput64` / `NativeMethods.SendInput` instead of crashing the TCP receiver loop (`SocketStuff.MainTCPRoutine`).
- When showing `DotForm` in `FormHelper.WndProc` (`case 0x407:`), `MouseWithoutBordersHelper` should not call 32-bit `NativeMethods.SendInput` with a 32-byte `INPUT` struct (`FieldOffset(4)`) on a 64-bit OS.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`SocketStuff.MainTCPRoutine` repeatedly crashes with an unhandled `System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException (0x8007007A: The data area passed to a system call is too small)` thrown from `Windows.UI.Input.Preview.Injection.InputInjector.InjectMouseInput`, which immediately drops the active TCP connection and triggers an endless disconnect/reconnect storm:

```text
[Error] SocketStuff.cs::MainTCPRoutine::1509
    System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException (0x8007007A): The data area passed to a system call is too small. (0x8007007A)
   at Windows.UI.Input.Preview.Injection.InputInjector.InjectMouseInput(IEnumerable`1 input)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.InputSimulation.SendInputEx(INPUT input)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.InputSimulation.MoveMouseRelative(Int32 x, Int32 y)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Core.CommonReceiver.ProcessMousePackage(DATA package, TcpSk tcp)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Core.CommonReceiver.ProcessPackage(DATA package, TcpSk tcp)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.SocketStuff.MainTCPRoutine(TcpSk tcp, Boolean bClient)
```

### Root Cause Analysis

Inspection of `main` reveals three compounding defects in `InitAndCleanup.cs` and `InputSimulation.cs` (related to tracking overview #51077 and #43292):

1. **Initialization probe in `InitAndCleanup.Init()` never actually tests `Injector.InjectMouseInput` ([`InitAndCleanup.cs:112-128`](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/InitAndCleanup.cs#L112-L128)):**
   ```csharp
   try
   {
       InputSimulation.Injector = InputInjector.TryCreate();
       if (InputSimulation.Injector != null)
       {
           InputSimulation.MoveMouseRelative(0, 0);        // (1) Called while InjectMouseInputAvailable is still false!
           NativeMethods.InjectMouseInputAvailable = true; // (2) Set to true AFTER MoveMouseRelative(0, 0)
       }
   }
   catch (EntryPointNotFoundException)                     // (3) Only catches EntryPointNotFoundException, not COMException
   {
       NativeMethods.InjectMouseInputAvailable = false;
       Logger.Log($"{nameof(NativeMethods.InjectMouseInputAvailable)} = false");
   }

   bool dummy = Setting.Values.DrawMouseEx;
   Common.Is64bitOS = IntPtr.Size == 8;                    // (4) Initialized AFTER MoveMouseRelative(0, 0)
   ```
   - Because `NativeMethods.InjectMouseInputAvailable` defaults to `false` and is only set to `true` **after** `InputSimulation.MoveMouseRelative(0, 0)` returns, the test call in `Init()` takes the `else` branch in `InputSimulation.SendInputEx` and never invokes `Injector.InjectMouseInput(...)` at all.
   - Furthermore, `Common.Is64bitOS = IntPtr.Size == 8` is set on line 128 **after** `MoveMouseRelative(0, 0)` on line 117, so the probe call in `Init()` executes the 32-bit `SendInput` branch with the wrong `INPUT` struct layout on 64-bit Windows.
   - Finally, the `catch` clause only catches `EntryPointNotFoundException`, whereas `InputInjector.TryCreate()` / `InjectMouseInput()` throws `COMException` (e.g., `0x8007007A` or `0x80070005`) when UWP input injection fails.

2. **No `COMException` fallback in `InputSimulation.SendInputEx()` ([`InputSimulation.cs:82-103`](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Class/InputSimulation.cs#L82-L103)):**
   - When `NativeMethods.InjectMouseInputAvailable` is `true`, `SendInputEx` calls `Injector.InjectMouseInput(...)` without a `try/catch` block.
   - Whenever `InjectMouseInput` throws `COMException` (either immediately on Windows 10 `10.0.19045` or transiently during a desktop/cursor state change), the unhandled exception propagates out of `ProcessMousePackage` into `SocketStuff.MainTCPRoutine`, terminating the TCP session.

### Proposed Fix

1. In `src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/InitAndCleanup.cs`:
   - Initialize `Common.Is64bitOS = IntPtr.Size == 8;` **before** the `InputInjector` probe block.
   - Set `NativeMethods.InjectMouseInputAvailable = true;` **before** calling `InputSimulation.MoveMouseRelative(0, 0);` so that `SendInputEx` actually exercises `Injector.InjectMouseInput`.
   - Catch `COMException` (in addition to `EntryPointNotFoundException`) in the initialization block to set `NativeMethods.InjectMouseInputAvailable = false` and log the fallback.
2. In `src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Class/InputSimulation.cs`:
   - Extract or wrap the `Injector.InjectMouseInput(...)` call in `SendInputEx` with a `try/catch (COMException ex)` handler that disables `NativeMethods.InjectMouseInputAvailable`, logs the exception once, and falls back to `NativeMethods.SendInput64` / `NativeMethods.SendInput` so the active mouse movement and TCP connection are never interrupted.

### Additional Information

- OS version: Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (`10.0.19045`) x64 & Windows 11 x64
- .NET version: .NET 10.0
- Running as admin: Yes (User mode, `UseService = false`)

title: Command Palette: inherited Windows App SDK runtime directory can crash launched apps
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

Command Palette's Windows App SDK runtime-directory override is inherited by launched applications. This report concerns launch-environment compatibility, not a request for an application-specific exception.

Logitech G HUB is one confirmed reproduction. Other applications have not been tested, so this report does not claim that every Windows App SDK application is affected.

1. With PowerToys running, open an affected application using its original Windows Start menu shortcut. Confirm that it opens normally.
2. Close the application's main window. For the confirmed G HUB reproduction, its existing background tray process and services were left running.
3. Open Command Palette and search for the same application.
4. Select the original application entry and press Enter.
5. Command Palette dismisses, but the application window does not appear. Windows records a crash in the launched process.
6. Open the same original shortcut from the Start menu again. The application opens normally.

Confirmed example:
- Logitech G HUB product version: 2026.6.981214
- Original shortcut:
  C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Logi\Logitech G HUB.lnk
- Shortcut target:
  C:\Program Files\LGHUB\system_tray\lghub_system_tray.exe
- Shortcut arguments: none
- Shortcut working directory:
  C:\Program Files\LGHUB\system_tray

Use the original application entry when reproducing this, not the environment-clearing workaround described below.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Launching an application's original shortcut from Command Palette should work as it does from the Start menu.

Command Palette's application-specific Windows App SDK runtime-directory configuration should not influence runtime or resource resolution inside unrelated launched applications.

Any fix should preserve Command Palette's own runtime configuration while preventing inappropriate inheritance by child applications. It should not require application-specific exceptions or changes to the user's global environment.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Command Palette finds the application and starts its launcher, but the launched process crashes before the application window opens.

The failure is not a missing executable or invalid shortcut. The same original shortcut works from the Start menu.

In the confirmed reproduction, Windows Application Error records show:

Application: lghub_system_tray.exe
Application version reported by Windows: 2026.6.1214.0
Faulting module: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll
Module version: 3.1.5.0
Exception code: 0xC000027B
Fault offset: 0x00000000004051C5

The corresponding Windows Error Reporting signature reports:
Module: combase.dll
Error: 0x80004002 (E_NOINTERFACE)

A crash timestamp matched the application's launch timestamp in Command Palette's history.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

Environment where the problem was observed

| Component                               | Version/details             |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Windows                                 | Windows 11 Enterprise, 26H2 |
| Windows build                            |26300.9457                  |
| Architecture                             |x64                         |
| PowerToys                                |0.101.2362.0                |
| Command Palette package                  |0.12.12365.0                |
| Command Palette executable file version  |0.12.2608.24005             |
| PowerToys installation scope             |Per-user                    |
| Controlled comparison | Non-elevated PowerShell |

Environment comparison

The running Command Palette process contained:

`MICROSOFT_WINDOWSAPPRUNTIME_BASE_DIRECTORY=<Command Palette installation directory>\`

That variable was absent from:

- Windows Explorer’s environment.
- The existing, working G HUB tray process’s environment.
- Persistent Windows user and machine environment settings.

The runtime DLL metadata also differed:  Microsoft.WindowsAppRuntime.dll  reported product version 2.0 in Command Palette and 1.5 in G HUB.

Controlled isolation test

The exact same original shortcut was launched using  Process.Start  with  UseShellExecute = true. Only the test process’s runtime-base-directory environment variable was changed.

| Test condition | Observed result |
| - | - |
| Variable set to Command Palette’s runtime directory | Launcher exited with 0xC000027B; matching WinUI crash recorded |
| Variable removed from the test process’s environment | Launcher exited with 0; G HUB’s main window opened |

The original environment value was restored afterward. No shortcut arguments, working directories, installed files, or G HUB background processes were changed between these launches.

This isolates the inherited variable as sufficient to trigger the failure in the confirmed application; it does not establish exactly which internal runtime operation fails.

Verified workaround

A separate launcher clears the variable only in its own environment, then opens the original application shortcut:

```console
@echo off
setlocal
set "MICROSOFT_WINDOWSAPPRUNTIME_BASE_DIRECTORY="
start "" "<full path to the original application shortcut.lnk>"
endlocal
```

This workaround successfully launched the confirmed application even when the wrapper inherited Command Palette’s runtime override. It was also confirmed working through Command Palette itself.

Command Palette’s own environment and Windows user/machine environment settings were left unchanged.

Relevant source references

- [PowerToys AppCommand.cs](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.Apps/AppCommand.cs): the inspected source launches desktop applications using Process.Start  with  UseShellExecute = true .
- [PowerToys KeyboardManagerViewModel.cs](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/ViewModels/KeyboardManagerViewModel.cs): existing PowerToys code explicitly clears the same variable before launching Keyboard Manager editors.
- [Windows App SDK base-directory initializer](https://github.com/microsoft/WindowsAppSDK/blob/main/dev/Common/WindowsAppRuntimeBaseDirectoryAutoInitializer.cs) and [runtime catalog code](https://github.com/microsoft/WindowsAppSDK/blob/main/dev/UndockedRegFreeWinRT/catalog.cpp): the inspected upstream source explicitly documents inheritance of this variable and includes a process ownership stamp/check.

The SDK source references [microsoft/WindowsAppSDK#5987](https://github.com/microsoft/WindowsAppSDK/issues/5987). Which released runtime versions include that protection was not verified. These references are relevant for triage, not proof that updating PowerToys alone will resolve compatibility with every older child runtime.

Logitech G HUB 2026.6.981214

G HUB tray executable version reported by Windows crash records:
2026.6.1214.0

Bundled Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll file version:
3.1.5.0

### Steps to reproduce

Title: Feature Request: Prevent text shifting ("jumping") in Dock Panel metrics due to digit count changes

Description:
Currently, the system monitoring widgets in the Command Palette's Dock-panel (preview) dynamically resize based on the text length. When a metric changes its magnitude/digit count (e.g., dropping from "10.5 Kbps" to "9.5 Kbps" or jumping from "99%" to "100%"), the entire row of widgets shifts back and forth. This constant "jumping" is visually distracting. The use of standard proportional fonts exacerbates the issue.

Proposed Solutions:

Implement Fixed-Width Containers: Set a fixed width for each monitoring widget (or provide a "Fixed width" toggle) so the container doesn't resize when the digit count changes.

Text Padding: Pad the numeric values with leading spaces (or zeros) to maintain a consistent string length regardless of the magnitude.

Monospace Font: Default to a monospace font for numeric values to prevent micro-shifts when digits change (e.g., from '0' to '1').

Варіант українською

body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version
0.101.2362

### Installation method
WinGet (per-user)

### Running as admin
No

### Area(s) with issue?
FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce
1. Enable FancyZones → *Move newly created windows to their last known zone*.
2. Snap Autodesk 3ds Max 2027 into a zone and close it.
3. Start 3ds Max again.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior
Only the 3ds Max main window is moved to its last zone.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The **MAXScript Debugger** dialog, which 3ds Max normally never shows at startup, stays on screen stretched to the zone's size. Its window is ownerless `#32770`, style `0x94CF0044`.

Root cause, from WinEvent traces of 11 launches:

- During startup, 3ds Max **shows the MAXScript Debugger and hides it again within 1–3 ms**.
- FancyZones handles the `EVENT_OBJECT_SHOW`, sees a visible, unowned, processable window of `3dsmax.exe`, and snaps it.
- The snap uses `SetWindowPlacement(WPF_ASYNCWINDOWPLACEMENT, SW_RESTORE)`. 3ds Max's UI thread processes that request *after* it has hidden the dialog, so the dialog is shown again.
- The debugger HWND is also stored in `AppZoneHistory` as the app's zoned window. While it exists, `IsAnotherWindowOfApplicationInstanceZoned` blocks history updates for the real main window for the rest of the session.

| Launches | Setting | Debugger snapped | Debugger left visible at zone size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | on | 9/9 | 4/9 |
| 2 | off | 0/2 | 0/2 |

Likely the same family as #22515 (TickTick blank window) and #33450 / #29145 / #30169 (secondary windows snapped into the app's zone).

Autodesk 3ds Max 2027 (with V-Ray, Corona, Forest Pack and RailClone plug-ins), Windows 11 26300

title: Tabbed Window Grouping with Split Screen
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

The proposed functionality uses the behavior of the software "Groupy 2" as a reference, which allows users to drag and group Windows applications into tabs within a single main container. However, PowerToys would expand upon this by adding a fundamental feature that Groupy 2 lacks: the ability to split the viewing area within that same grouped window. Users could grab a tab and snap it side-by-side with another tab inside the same container. The expected behavior is that the main window controls (minimize, maximize, restore, and move) would affect the entire group simultaneously. If two windows are split side-by-side within this group, clicking "minimize" would collapse both with a single click.

### Scenario when this would be used?

For power users, managing individual windows requires excessive clicking and disrupts productivity. A practical use case is for day traders managing multiple accounts, who need to keep two or more instances of trading platforms (like Profit or MetaTrader) open side-by-side. Currently, Windows forces users to minimize each instance independently. With this feature, they could group the terminals into a single window (like Groupy 2), split them side-by-side for simultaneous viewing, and minimize them all as a single application to quickly clear the desktop. This naturally applies to many other scenarios, such as grouping multiple spreadsheet files into tabs and easily switching between them.

(https://1drv.ms/v/c/fd0b5146bb1c804b/IQBCpba7bJWBRpTH3acv2o8_AfOIudUJlDBQSdNOjzz8w0o?e=mZ5aEa)

(Note: I tried to attach a video demonstrating this, but the upload failed.)

### Supporting information

The primary usability reference for the tab system is Stardock's "Groupy 2," which proves the immense utility of grouping applications in Windows but falls short by not allowing two tabs to be viewed simultaneously. The reference for the internal split-view is the Microsoft Edge browser, which introduced a native "Split screen" feature for viewing two pages side-by-side within the same window. Combining Groupy 2's tab mechanics with Edge's split-screen capabilities at the OS level would be an indispensable productivity innovation for Windows.

title: PDF Preview Handler crashes (0xe0434352) when Explorer previews a PDF while another app's Medium-IL preview host already uses it
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.101.2362.0 - Stable ### Installation method PowerToys auto-update ### Area(s) with issue? File Explorer: Preview Pane ### Steps to reproduce 1. Make sure no `prevhost.exe` is running (close Explorer windows and apps that show file previews). 2. Preview a PDF in an application that hosts preview handlers at Medium integrity level. I used the preview pane of Everything 1.5a; its `prevhost.exe` runs at Medium IL. 3. Keep that preview open and select a PDF in File Explorer with the preview pane enabled. The order matters. If Explorer previews a PDF first, both previews work side by side until every preview host has exited. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The Explorer preview pane shows the PDF, no matter whether another application previews a PDF at the same time. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The `PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe` started for Explorer dies with an unhandled .NET exception and Explorer shows no preview. Windows Error Reporting is disabled on this machine, so Windows shows the legacy dialog instead of a WER report (translated from German): > PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe - Application Error > The exception unknown software exception (0xe0434352) occurred in the application at location 0x00007FFD9D7041CA. The PdfPrevHandler log of the Explorer preview host shows `Failed to create resize event for PdfPreviewHandler` on every resize (log excerpt below). ### Additional Information Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9457 **Two preview hosts with different integrity levels** While the crash happens, two `prevhost.exe` processes have `PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandlerCpp.dll` loaded: | Client | prevhost.exe started for | IL | Parent window of the handler exe | |---|---|---|---| | Everything | `{A5A41CC7-02CB-41D4-8C9B-9087040D6098}` (PowerToys PDF handler) | Medium | `EVERYTHING_PREVIEW_HANDLER` (Everything.exe) | | Explorer preview pane | `{914FEED8-267A-4BAA-B8AA-21E233792679}` ("Microsoft Preview Creator", shell32.dll) | Low | `Shell Preview Extension Host Previewer` (prevhost.exe) | **Root cause** Both instances use the same session-wide named event `Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-5a2f162a-f728-45fe-8bda-ef3d5e434ce7`: - `PdfPreviewHandler::PdfPreviewHandler()` calls `CreateEvent(nullptr, false, false, PDF_PREVIEW_RESIZE_EVENT)` with the default security descriptor. - `PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe` opens it in `Common.UI.NativeEventWaiter.WaitForEventLoop` with `new EventWaitHandle(false, EventResetMode.AutoReset, eventName)`. That runs on a background thread without try/catch. When the Medium-IL host creates the event first, the event gets the default Medium mandatory label. The Low-IL instance is then denied access by the no-write-up policy: - C++ side: `CreateEvent` returns NULL, so the handler logs `Failed to create resize event` and continues. - .NET side: the `EventWaitHandle` constructor throws `UnauthorizedAccessException` on the background thread. The exception is unhandled and the process terminates with 0xe0434352. When the Low-IL host creates the event first, it gets a Low label and the Medium instance can open it. That is why the order matters. The event lives as long as any process holds a handle, and the C++ handler never closes `m_resizeEvent` (the destructor has no `CloseHandle`), so every preview host keeps it alive until it exits. **Verified on the affected machine** `repro-lowil-event.ps1` (below) creates the event in a Medium-IL PowerShell and opens it with an impersonated Low-IL token, the same way `NativeEventWaiter` does (output translated from German): ``` low IL: System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path 'Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-test-…' is denied. control, fresh event opened at low IL: OK ``` While the Everything preview host held the real event (Medium label), opening `Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-5a2f162a-…` with a Low-IL token failed the same way; a Medium token worked. No dump or stack trace is available because WER is disabled on this machine. **Still present on main** `src/common/Common.UI/NativeEventWaiter.cs` and `src/modules/previewpane/PdfPreviewHandler/Program.cs` are unchanged on `main`. `FileExplorerDllExporter/PreviewHandler.cpp` from #50252 still calls `CreateEvent(nullptr, false, false, resizeEvent)` with a global name and never closes the handle. The other preview handlers (Markdown, SVG, Monaco, G-code, Bgcode, QOI) use the same pattern and are probably affected as well. **Suggested fix** - Give each handler instance its own event name, for example by passing it to the exe as an argument. That also fixes a second problem of the shared auto-reset event: with two running instances, a resize signal wakes only one of them. - Alternatively, create the event with a security descriptor that carries a Low mandatory label (SDDL `S:(ML;;NW;;;LW)`) so Low and Medium instances can both open it. - In `NativeEventWaiter`, handle a failure to open the event instead of letting the background thread terminate the process. - Close `m_resizeEvent` in the handler's destructor. Possibly the same cause: #39851 (same dialog, closed because it could not be reproduced).

body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.101.2362

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

# [Bug] Command Palette terminates silently when launching an elevated process (terminal profile / Ctrl+Enter)

## Microsoft PowerToys version

`0.101.2362.0`

## Installation method

winget (`Microsoft.PowerToys`) — confirmed latest, `winget upgrade --id Microsoft.PowerToys` reports *"No available upgrade found"*

## Command Palette package version

`Microsoft.CommandPalette 0.12.12365.0`

## Running PowerToys as admin

No — PowerToys and CmdPal both run **unelevated**. The CmdPal log confirms this on every launch:

```
Is elevated:           no
```

## Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

## Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure PowerToys is running **unelevated** (default) and Command Palette is enabled.
2. Open Command Palette (hotkey here was `Alt+Space`).
3. Search for the terminal, e.g. `terminal` / `终端`.
4. Invoke it **as administrator** (elevated terminal profile, or the `Ctrl+Enter` "run as admin" action).
5. Observe.

## ✔️ Expected Behavior

An elevated terminal window opens (this part **does** work), and Command Palette **stays running** so it can be used again.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

* The elevated terminal **does open successfully**.
* Command Palette **terminates silently** immediately afterwards.
* The Command Palette hotkey then does nothing, because the process is gone.
* Recovery requires restarting PowerToys (or relaunching the `Microsoft.CommandPalette` MSIX app).

### Evidence that this is a clean self-exit, not a crash

This appears to be **different from** #38460 (`MoAppCrash` with a faulting module in `ntdll.dll` / `combase.dll`). Here there is **no crash at all**:

* **No crash record in the Application event log.** Queried the last 2000 Application events filtered on `CmdPal|CommandPalette|MoAppCrash` — **zero** matches.
* **No Windows Error Reporting entry** for `Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe`.
* **No exception, stack trace, or `[Error]` entry in the CmdPal log.** The log simply stops.
* The last log line is the search that led to the launch, then nothing:

```
[02:35:45.7372048] [Info] SearchQuery.cs::TryExecuteFallbackQuery::269
    Retrying search with implicit filename wildcard matching. Reason=primary query returned zero rows, Query="zhong'd"
```

After that line: no further output, no shutdown message, no error. The process is just gone.

* The PowerToys main process (`PowerToys.exe`) **remains alive and responsive** — only the CmdPal process exits.

### Process state immediately after

```
PowerToys            22616   Responding=True
Microsoft.CmdPal.UI  —       (not running)
```

## Control test — what is NOT the cause

To narrow this down I ran a separate test: while PowerToys/CmdPal were healthy, I launched an elevated process **from outside** CmdPal (`Start-Process -Verb RunAs`):

* Elevated process created successfully.
* CmdPal stayed alive for the full 30-second observation window (same PID throughout).
* **Zero new lines** in the CmdPal log — it was not affected at all.

So it is **not** "the presence of an elevated process on the system" that kills CmdPal. It is specifically **CmdPal's own elevation code path** when it spawns the elevated child itself.

I also confirmed that **non-elevated** launching is fine:

* Normal (non-elevated) terminal launch from Command Palette → Command Palette keeps working.

This isolates the bug to the **elevation path only**.

## Relation to #38460

#38460 was reported on `0.90.0` and closed via PR #38493, whose fix was:

> Regardless of how it happens, I've defaulted us to just *not enabling the winget built-in*. That's the simplest solution here.

That change avoided a *startup* crash caused by failing to initialize WinGet (which happens when running elevated). It did **not** address the case where an **unelevated** CmdPal launches an **elevated** child process.

This report is that remaining case, still reproducible on `0.101.2362.0` — roughly 11 minor versions after the original fix. It may be a regression, or the original fix may have only masked part of the problem.

Note: in this environment the **WinGet built-in is enabled** (`"WinGet": { "IsEnabled": true }` in CmdPal `settings.json`), so if the root cause is still WinGet COM initialization failing on an elevated code path, that would be consistent.

## Other software

* Windows 11, build `10.0.26100.6584` (24H2)
* Locale: `zh-CN`
* .NET runtime reported by CmdPal: `10.0.11`
* Windows Terminal installed (`wt.exe`, Store version)
* UAC: `ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin = 0` (elevate without prompting), `EnableLUA = 1`, `PromptOnSecureDesktop = 0`
* Account is a member of `Administrators` but runs with a filtered token (standard UAC admin-approval mode); the built-in `Administrator` account is disabled.

## Suggested direction

Per @zadjii-msft's comment on #38460:

> We probably need to add some additional checks throughout the launcher code to make sure CmdPal is starting unelevated

…the elevation path still seems able to take down the whole palette process. Two things worth checking:

1. Whether the elevated-launch helper (whatever spawns the elevated child) can fail in a way that terminates the parent instead of surfacing an error.
2. Whether WinGet-related initialization is still on that code path (given PR #38493's fix was to disable the WinGet built-in rather than fix elevation).

Ideally a failed/unsupported elevation should surface an error to the user and leave Command Palette running.

### Steps to reproduce

An extension command that activates another application can leave the target flashing in the taskbar or visible without keyboard focus.

`PowerToysRootPageService.OnPerformCommand` calls `SetActiveExtension`, but `SetActiveExtension` only calls `CoAllowSetForegroundWindow` when `extension != _activeExtension`. Commands invoked while staying in the same extension therefore reuse an earlier foreground grant.

Foreground grants are revocable. Windows documents that input directed to another process, or a subsequent grant to a different process, can revoke the permission. The active extension's identity is not sufficient to determine whether its permission remains valid.

title: PowerToys general settings lost on every restart unless manually exited from tray
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.101.2362 - Stable

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

General, Settings, System tray interaction

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have PowerToys running normally with custom General settings (specific modules enabled/disabled, `enable_quick_access` toggled, etc.) already saved to `settings.json`.
2. Restart or shut down Windows through any normal path (Start menu, `shutdown.exe`, etc.) **without** first manually exiting PowerToys via its tray icon's "Exit" command.
3. After the machine comes back up, inspect `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\settings.json`.

Result: the file is frequently found reduced to an empty `{}` (or the runner logs `apply_general_settings: {}` on the next launch), and all General settings — including which modules are enabled — revert to PowerToys' compiled-in defaults.

This was narrowed down through the following controlled tests:
- **Ruled out restart speed / OS shutdown timeout**: raised `HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\WaitToKillAppTimeout` and `HungAppTimeout` to `20000` (4x default). No effect — corruption still occurred. This indicates the app acknowledges the shutdown request quickly (so Windows never applies the hung-app wait at all) while an asynchronous settings save is still in flight, rather than PowerToys genuinely running out of time.
- **Ruled out elevation/auto-elevation**: reproduced with "Always run as administrator" disabled and PowerToys running non-elevated.
- **Ruled out AV/EDR or external interference**: no related entries in Windows Defender / EDR protection history. Task Scheduler's own history shows PowerToys' own startup task being deleted and recreated each boot, seemingly as routine self-managed housekeeping rather than external tampering, and this is independent of the settings corruption.
- **Confirmed the corruption happens at shutdown of the *previous* session, not at the next startup**: disabled "Run at startup" entirely, left PowerToys running, restarted, and checked `settings.json` before ever relaunching PowerToys — it was already empty.
- **Confirmed a clean manual Exit (tray icon → Exit) never corrupts the file**, across multiple repeated tests.
- **Confirmed a "graceful" programmatic close does *not* reproduce the safety of a manual Exit**: a Task Scheduler task triggered on Event ID 1074 (System log, source User32 — logged when a shutdown/restart is initiated, before the OS notifies applications) running `taskkill /IM PowerToys.exe` (no `/F`, i.e. a `WM_CLOSE` request rather than a forced kill) still corrupted `settings.json` on the very first test.

This suggests the tray menu's "Exit" command invokes a distinct, apparently-synchronous save-then-quit routine, while any other close signal (`WM_CLOSE` from `taskkill`, or the OS's own session-ending notification, visible in the runner log as `Runner WM_DESTROY, system_session_ending=true`) hits a different, race-prone save path.

Relevant runner log excerpt (from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\Logs`), showing a boot where settings were lost:
```
[...] [info] runner logger is initialized
[...] [info] apply_general_settings: {}
[...] [warning] apply_general_settings: show_theme_adaptive_tray_icon not found in config
[...] [info] Runner is starting. Elevated=true openOobe=false openScoobe=false showRestartNotificationAfterUpdate=false
[...] [info] start_enabled_powertoys: Enabling powertoy AlwaysOnTop
[...] (all modules reset to default enabled/disabled state)
```
And from the end of the preceding session:
```
[...] [info] Runner WM_DESTROY, system_session_ending=true
```
compared to a manually-triggered restart in the same log, which preserved settings correctly:
```
[...] [info] Runner WM_DESTROY, system_session_ending=false
```

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

`settings.json` (and the enabled/disabled state of all modules) should persist across a normal Windows restart/shutdown exactly as reliably as it does after a manual "Exit" from the tray icon.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`settings.json` is intermittently truncated to an empty `{}` whenever PowerToys is closed by anything other than the tray icon's "Exit" command — including a normal OS restart/shutdown and a "graceful" external `WM_CLOSE` (e.g. via `taskkill` without `/F`) — causing all General settings to silently revert to defaults on the next launch. This is not fixed by increasing the OS shutdown timeout, is not related to elevation, and is not caused by antivirus/EDR interference.

title: [CmdPal Dock] Bands disappear from secondary monitor after Modern Standby
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2373.0 — Preview

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Command Palette Dock on two monitors.
2. Pin external extension bands to the Center region on both monitors. 
3. Allow the machine to enter Modern Standby after an idle timeout.
4. Wake the machine with the keyboard.
5. Intermittently, extensions disappear from the secondary monitor's dock.
6. The same extensions continue working on the primary monitor, and their extension processes remain alive.
7. Restart the Command Palette Dock.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

When a secondary monitor reconnects during resume, its dock should retain and render all saved Start, Center, and End bands.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The two external bands in the secondary monitor's Center region sometimes disappear after resume. They remain visible and functional on the primary monitor.

The bands are not removed from the saved configuration. Restarting the Command Palette Dock causes them to reappear.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

- The affected extension processes remained running and responsive.
- The extensions logged no errors or exceptions.
- Windows recorded no corresponding application crash.
- The saved `DockSettings` configuration still contained the affected commands under `CenterBands` for `\\.\DISPLAY2`, the Windows device name for the secondary
monitor.
- Restarting the dock rebuilt the saved bands successfully.

This appears related to #49086, #49668, and #49604, but this case specifically affects saved extension-provided bands on the secondary dock while the extensions
remain healthy and usable from the primary dock.

### Likely lifecycle issue

Current `main` in `DockWindowManager.cs` waits only 400 milliseconds before reconciling a monitor change:

```csharp
private static readonly TimeSpan MonitorsChangedDebounceInterval =
  TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(400);
```

`SyncDocksToSettingsCore` then closes and disposes any dock whose monitor is temporarily absent. Because this resume transition lasted approximately 1.95
seconds, the secondary dock was destroyed before the monitor returned.

A possible minimal mitigation would be a debounce longer than the observed resume transition:

```diff
-private static readonly TimeSpan MonitorsChangedDebounceInterval =
-    TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(400);
+// Resume can transiently remove a display while the graphics stack re-enumerates it.
+private static readonly TimeSpan MonitorsChangedDebounceInterval =
+    TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3);
```

### Other Software

One thing to note is that both my monitors use different port types, one is DP and the other is HDMI which is why the displays take longer than usual to get detected on my Win11 environment.

### Microsoft PowerToys version

0.101.2362.0

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update / installer (per-user)

### Running as admin

No / Unknown

### Area(s) with issue?

General / Runner (WinUI3Apps - Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start PowerToys.exe (e.g. via Start Menu shortcut or startup task).
2. The application exits immediately after launch — it does not stay running and no usable window appears.
3. Windows Error Reporting logs an application crash pointing at `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll`.

This is a consistent crash-on-launch: PowerToys never reaches a running/usable state.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

PowerToys should start normally and remain running in the system tray.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

PowerToys.exe crashes with exception code `0xc000027b` faulting in `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll` and the application exits immediately after start.

### Other Software

N/A

---

**Windows Error Reporting details**

```
Faulting application name: PowerToys.exe, version: 0.101.2362.0, time stamp: 0x6a8d2e3f
Faulting module name: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll, version: 3.2.2.0, time stamp: 0x94acc299
Exception code: 0xc000027b
Fault offset: 0x00000000003ad79d
Faulting process id: 0x5948
Faulting application start time: 0x1DD43E065F26332
Faulting application path: C:\Users\jcanf\AppData\Local\PowerToys\PowerToys.exe
Faulting module path: C:\Users\jcanf\AppData\Local\PowerToys\Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll
Report Id: e23aa06c-1749-4aec-8324-6e94c15f640c

Faulting package-relative application ID: 
```

**Windows version info**

- Edition: Windows 11 Pro
- Version: 25H2
- Installed on: 1/22/2026
- OS build: 26200.9445
- Experience: Windows Feature Experience Pack 1000.26100.360.0

### Additional Information

The application exits right after starting — this is not an intermittent crash during use, it happens on every launch attempt. This crash signature (exception `0xc000027b` faulting in `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll`) has appeared in other PowerToys issues (e.g. #36786, #36028) tied to WinUI3/XAML islands failing to initialize correctly, sometimes related to per-user vs. system-wide install conflicts or missing/mismatched Windows App SDK runtime components. Will attach logs from `%localappdata%\Microsoft\PowerToys` if needed.

title: Advanced Paste: AI custom actions fail after exactly 100 seconds because HttpClient.Timeout is never configured, making local model providers unusable for anything but short inputs
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Advanced Paste

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Settings > Advanced Paste > Model providers, add an Ollama provider
   pointing at a self-hosted Ollama server.

2. Select a model whose generation for a realistic input exceeds 100 seconds.
   Two easy ways to hit this:
     a. Any 12B-class model on consumer GPUs, with an input of roughly
        2,000 words or more, using a transformation that regenerates its
        input (redaction, rewriting, reformatting, translation).
     b. Any reasoning model with thinking enabled, where hidden reasoning
        tokens inflate total generation well beyond the visible output.

3. Create a custom action under Settings > Advanced Paste > Custom actions
   with any prompt that transforms the whole input.

4. Copy content to the clipboard, press Win+Shift+V, and run the custom action.

5. Wait.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

One of the following:

- The action completes, however long generation takes, or
- A timeout is configurable per model provider in Settings, so that local
  inference can be given a realistic ceiling, or
- At minimum, the failure message identifies the timeout as the cause and
  states the limit, so the user can tell a timeout apart from a connection
  failure, an unavailable model, or a malformed request.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

After approximately 100 seconds, the Advanced Paste window shows:

    The paste operation was cancelled

The message is identical to what a user sees after pressing the cancel (X)
button, and gives no indication that a timeout occurred. Nothing in the UI
suggests the limit exists or what it is.

The module log records the real cause:

      [14:32:21.0924623] [Error] CustomActionTransformService.cs::TransformAsync::115
      CustomActionTransformService.TransformAsync failed
      System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException (-2146233029): The request was canceled due to the configured HttpClient.Timeout of 100 seconds elapsing.
      Inner exception: 
      System.TimeoutException (-2146233083): The operation was canceled.


with the failure originating in:

      Stack trace: 
      at System.Net.Http.HttpClient.HandleFailure(Exception e, Boolean telemetryStarted, HttpResponseMessage response, CancellationTokenSource cts, CancellationToken cancellationToken,  CancellationTokenSource pendingRequestsCts)
      at System.Net.Http.HttpClient.<SendAsync>g__Core|83_0(HttpRequestMessage request, HttpCompletionOption completionOption, CancellationTokenSource cts, Boolean disposeCts,  CancellationTokenSource pendingRequestsCts, CancellationToken originalCancellationToken)
      at OllamaSharp.OllamaApiClient.SendToOllamaAsync(HttpRequestMessage requestMessage, OllamaRequest ollamaRequest, HttpCompletionOption completionOption, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
      at OllamaSharp.OllamaApiClient.ChatAsync(ChatRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)+MoveNext()
      at OllamaSharp.OllamaApiClient.ChatAsync(ChatRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)+System.Threading.Tasks.Sources.IValueTaskSource<System.Boolean>.GetResult()
      at OllamaSharp.IAsyncEnumerableExtensions.StreamToEndAsync[Tin,Tout](IAsyncEnumerable`1 stream, IAppender`2 appender, Action`1 itemCallback)
      at OllamaSharp.IAsyncEnumerableExtensions.StreamToEndAsync[Tin,Tout](IAsyncEnumerable`1 stream, IAppender`2 appender, Action`1 itemCallback)
      at OllamaSharp.OllamaApiClient.Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient.GetResponseAsync(IEnumerable`1 messages, ChatOptions options, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
      
and reaching it through:

      at Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient.GetResponseAsync(IEnumerable`1 messages, ChatOptions options, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
            at Microsoft.SemanticKernel.ChatCompletion.ChatClientChatCompletionService.GetChatMessageContentsAsync(ChatHistory chatHistory, PromptExecutionSettings executionSettings, Kernel      kernel,    CancellationToken cancellationToken)
            at Microsoft.SemanticKernel.ChatCompletion.ChatCompletionServiceExtensions.GetChatMessageContentAsync(IChatCompletionService chatCompletionService, ChatHistory chatHistory,        PromptExecutionSettings executionSettings, Kernel kernel, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
            at AdvancedPaste.Services.CustomActions.SemanticKernelPasteProvider.ProcessPasteAsync(PasteAIRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken, IProgress`1 progress)
            at AdvancedPaste.Services.CustomActions.CustomActionTransformService.TransformAsync(String prompt, String inputText, Byte[] imageBytes, PasteAIConfig providerConfig, CancellationToken         cancellationToken, IProgress`1 progress)
         [14:32:21.0963950] [Error] OptionsViewModel.cs::ExecutePasteFormatAsync::784
             Error executing paste format

Logged sites:
    CustomActionTransformService.cs::TransformAsync::115
    OptionsViewModel.cs::ExecutePasteFormatAsync::784

I reproduced this five times on 2026-09-03 with identical exception text
every time.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

ROOT CAUSE

100 seconds is the default value of System.Net.Http.HttpClient.Timeout in
.NET. The failure occurring at exactly that value, rather than at any
PowerToys-specific number, indicates the timeout is simply inherited rather
than set anywhere on this code path.

That default is shaped for cloud APIs, which typically respond in seconds.
It is not a reasonable ceiling for local inference, where multi-minute
generations are ordinary.


WHY THIS MAKES LOCAL PROVIDERS UNUSABLE IN PRACTICE

Measured on my hardware, an RTX 3070 plus an RTX 2060, serving a 12B model
at Q4 through Ollama:

  Throughput (warm)     : ~37.5 tokens/sec
  Model load (cold)     : ~10.7 sec
  Model load (warm)     : ~0.5 sec

100 seconds therefore allows roughly 3,750 generated tokens, or about 2,800
words. Any Advanced Paste transformation that regenerates its input, which
is most of the useful ones, fails on documents above roughly 2,000 words.
On a cold start the usable budget is about 10 percent smaller again.

The practical effect is that Advanced Paste's AI features work with cloud
providers and quietly stop working with local ones once inputs pass a
threshold that is never disclosed to the user.


REASONING MODELS MAKE THE FAILURE INTERMITTENT

Models with thinking enabled by default emit hidden reasoning tokens that
count fully against the same budget. On the trivial prompt "Reply with the
single word: ready", a Gemma 4 12B produced:

  Run 1: 56 output tokens
  Run 2: 80 output tokens
  Run 3: 38 output tokens

to return the single word "ready" each time. That is a 2.1x spread on
byte-identical input, because reasoning length varies with sampling and
PowerToys does not override the model's default temperature.

Consequently the same clipboard content can succeed and fail alternately.
Intermittent failure is considerably worse than consistent failure here,
because it reads to the user as flakiness rather than as a limit, and there
is no way to discover the real constraint without reading the module log.


SUGGESTED FIXES, IN ORDER OF PREFERENCE

1. Expose a per-provider timeout in Settings > Advanced Paste > Model
   providers, alongside the existing endpoint and model fields. Local
   inference latency varies by orders of magnitude across hardware, so a
   fixed value cannot serve every user well.

2. Failing that, set a substantially longer default timeout when the
   selected provider is local, while leaving cloud providers as they are.

3. Independently of either, surface the underlying exception message in the
   UI rather than collapsing every failure into "The paste operation was
   cancelled". A user who cancels deliberately and a user who hits a
   100-second ceiling currently see the same string. Distinguishing them
   would have saved me several hours.


ENVIRONMENT

  PowerToys      : 0.101.2362.0
  Windows        : Windows 11 (25H2)
  Model server   : Ollama on a separate Linux host, reached over LAN
  GPUs           : NVIDIA RTX 3070 (8GB) + RTX 2060 (6GB)

Connectivity to the Ollama endpoint is confirmed working. Identical requests
issued directly to the same endpoint succeed; only the PowerToys path fails,
and only at the 100-second mark.

### Other Software

Ollama, self-hosted on a Linux host on the same LAN, reached over HTTP.
The same endpoint responds correctly to direct API requests, including for
generations well beyond 100 seconds, so the server is not the limiting
factor.

body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

General

### Steps to reproduce

1.Install PowerToys and launch it as a standard user (non-admin).

2.Open Settings and customize a few modules (e.g. FancyZones layout, Keyboard Manager shortcuts, PowerToys Run settings).

3.Quit PowerToys completely.

4.Relaunch PowerToys as administrator (right-click the system tray icon → "Restart as administrator").

5.Open Settings and observe that the customizations from step 2 are no longer present — a different set of settings is shown.

6.Restart the computer (or update PowerToys to a newer version), then try to launch PowerToys as administrator again.

7.Observe that PowerToys either fails to launch elevated, or the previously customized settings are reset to their defaults.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

A single source of truth is used for user settings — admin and non-admin modes share the same configuration.

Customized settings persist reliably across computer restarts and PowerToys updates.

Users do not need to worry about which privilege level PowerToys is currently running under; their customizations are always honored.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The admin and non-admin run modes use different configuration files, so the same module shows different settings depending on how PowerToys was launched.

After a computer restart or PowerToys update, PowerToys sometimes fails to launch as administrator. When it does launch, the previously customized settings are reset to their defaults, forcing the user to reconfigure everything from scratch.
